resources.string: Share of starting markers taken up
Starting markers left outside the cells: %1$s%%
If uptake is U percent of the starting pool and return is R percent of the taken-up share, the returned percentage of the starting pool is U × R / 100. The percentage left outside is 100 − U.

Near an excitatory synapse, an astrocyte process takes up some released glutamate. The astrocyte can convert some to glutamine and return it to the sending neuron for reuse. In this schematic, markers move from the space around the synapse into the astrocyte, then a share returns to the neuron. The returned markers represent recycling, not a new signal. The percentages are invented; they do not represent measured amounts, timing, or biological rates.
